subject: whale shark
title: The 5 Biggest Sharks Alive, Ranked (The Great White Is Only #4)

scenes.text: The five biggest sharks alive. The great white doesn't even make the top three.
Number five: the tiger shark. About eighteen feet, and it eats almost anything.
scenes.label: Tiger shark · ~18 ft

scenes.text: Number four: the great white. About twenty feet of the most famous teeth in the sea.
scenes.label: Great white · ~20 ft

scenes.text: Number three: the Greenland shark. Around twenty-one feet, slow, and it can live for centuries.
scenes.label: Greenland shark · ~21 ft

scenes.text: Number two: the basking shark. Around forty feet, swimming with its mouth wide open for plankton.
scenes.label: Basking shark · ~40 ft

scenes.text: Number one: the whale shark. About sixty feet, the biggest fish on Earth, and it eats some of the smallest food.
scenes.label: Whale shark · ~60 ft

description:
The five biggest living sharks, ranked by commonly accepted maximum length: tiger shark (about 5.5 m), great white (about 6 m), Greenland shark (about 6.4 m, reports up to 7.3 m), basking shark (about 12 m) and whale shark (about 18 m).
Maximum sizes for some deep-sea species, like the Pacific sleeper shark, are uncertain and they are often left off such lists. The two largest are both gentle filter feeders.
Which shark would you most want to see in the wild?
first_comment: The two biggest sharks eat plankton. Which shark would you put at number one for scariest, and what should we rank next?
